articles.title: Abstenção em Minas cai no 2º turno e favorece virada de Lula | G1
articles.standfirst: Índice passou de 22,81% para 20,33% entre os turnos. Cientistas políticos apontam mobilização de jovens e rejeição à família Bolsonaro como fatores que contribuíram para o aumento da participação e a virada de Lula no estado.
articles.summary: A queda da abstenção em Minas Gerais para 20,33% foi impulsionada pela mobilização de jovens e idosos, resultando na virada de Lula no segundo turno.
articles.body:
A abstenção eleitoral em Minas Gerais caiu de 22,81% no primeiro turno das eleições deste ano, em 4 de outubro, para 20,33% no segundo, realizado neste domingo (25).

De acordo com dados da Justiça Eleitoral, o número de mineiros que não compareceram às urnas passou de 3.735.098 para 3.327.941, uma redução de 10,9% no total de eleitores ausentes entre as duas etapas da votação. Ou seja, foram 407.157 eleitores a mais no segundo turno.

Apesar da queda de 2,48 pontos percentuais, mais de 3,3 milhões de eleitores mineiros deixaram de votar na disputa pela Presidência da República. O índice representa aproximadamente um em cada cinco eleitores do estado.

O aumento do comparecimento ocorreu em meio à virada do presidente Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) sobre Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) em Minas, único estado em que houve uma inversão na liderança entre os dois turnos .

Depois de ficar atrás do adversário na primeira etapa no estado, o petista conquistou 50,43% dos votos válidos, contra 49,57% do candidato do PL , uma diferença de 109.313 votos.

Para cientistas políticos ouvidos pela reportagem da TV Globo , a redução da abstenção e a mudança no resultado estão relacionadas à mobilização de jovens e idosos, ao engajamento nas redes sociais e ao crescimento da rejeição à possibilidade de retorno da família Bolsonaro ao Palácio do Planalto.

Esta reportagem aborda a abstenção em MG a partir dos seguintes pontos:

Grande BH e Norte de Minas tiveram papel decisivo

Rejeição à família Bolsonaro ajuda a explicar virada

Mesmo com queda, abstenção permanece elevada

Urna eletrônica nas eleições 2026 — Foto: Clara Sganzerla/g1

O cientista político Rudá Ricci , presidente do Instituto Cultiva, avalia que a mobilização de eleitores na Região Metropolitana de Belo Horizonte e no Norte de Minas foi determinante para a redução da abstenção e para o desempenho de Lula no estado.

Segundo ele, o movimento não ocorreu com a mesma intensidade em outras regiões mineiras, como o Sul de Minas e o Triângulo Mineiro.

Ricci também destaca o papel dos jovens na mobilização de familiares que haviam deixado de votar no primeiro turno, especialmente os idosos, para quem o voto é facultativo a partir dos 70 anos.

"Houve uma união muito peculiar e inusitada dos bem jovens com os bem idosos, que foram aqueles que não votaram no primeiro turno e que vieram aos montes nesse segundo turno", disse.

Na avaliação do especialista, a movimentação ganhou força nas três semanas que antecederam a votação e foi intensificada pela repercussão de um vídeo publicado pelo deputado federal Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) sobre o Nordeste e pelas participações de Flávio Bolsonaro nos debates da Band e da TV Globo .

Ricci considera que os episódios provocaram reações entre eleitores indecisos e contribuíram para ampliar a participação eleitoral, especialmente em Minas Gerais.

Para o cientista político Felipe Nunes , o resultado em Minas Gerais reflete uma mudança na forma como os eleitores avaliaram a disputa presidencial entre o primeiro e o segundo turnos.

Segundo ele, enquanto a primeira etapa funcionou como uma espécie de avaliação do governo Lula, a segunda passou a ser marcada pelo receio de um retorno da família Bolsonaro ao poder.

"Quando a eleição foi um sim ou não a favor do Lula, os mineiros votaram contra. Quando se tornou uma eleição plebiscitária em relação ao Flávio, os mineiros acabaram votando em favor da continuidade", explicou.

Em Minas, Lula recebeu 1,16 milhão de votos a mais no segundo turno, enquanto Flávio Bolsonaro ganhou aproximadamente 464 mil votos em relação à primeira etapa.

Nunes avalia que a mudança também está relacionada ao perfil do eleitorado mineiro, que, segundo ele, tende a tomar decisões de forma mais cautelosa e a manter a indefinição do voto por mais tempo.

"Nós, mineiros, somos muito cautelosos, cuidadosos com as decisões em geral e, na política, isso sempre foi verdade. [...] No fim, esse medo que aumentou no Brasil inteiro e também em Minas da volta da família Bolsonaro acabou pesando", afirmou.

O cientista político aponta ainda que a melhora na avaliação do governo federal durante a reta final da campanha contribuiu para a decisão de parte dos eleitores pela continuidade do atual presidente.

Outro fator destacado por Nunes foi a mobilização digital . Segundo ele, dados do Índice de Popularidade Digital (IPD) da Quaest mostram que Lula ultrapassou Flávio Bolsonaro em popularidade nas redes sociais durante o segundo turno, depois de encerrar a primeira etapa atrás do adversário.

O especialista cita, inclusive, a atuação do deputado federal mineiro André Janones (Avante) como um dos fatores que contribuíram para ampliar a mobilização virtual.

"Essa mobilização de rede, que, claro, mobilizou o jovem a levar os avós para votar, fazer os pais votarem, foi, como eu disse, inédita. Um padrão de comportamento que a gente não conhecia no Brasil recente", declarou.

Apesar da maior participação no segundo turno, Rudá Ricci considera que o índice de 20,33% de abstenção em Minas Gerais ainda é elevado, especialmente porque o voto é obrigatório para a maior parte do eleitorado brasileiro.

Para o cientista político, a ausência de uma parcela significativa dos eleitores revela dificuldades de identificação com os candidatos e com o sistema político.

"É uma falta de identidade com aquele que quer ser representante. Como vai ser representante se ele não quer me representar, ele quer se representar?", questionou.

Segundo Ricci, o problema vai além do desinteresse pelas eleições e está relacionado à percepção de que o debate político não aborda as necessidades cotidianas da população.

"Eu acho que isso não é exatamente uma crise da democracia. É uma crise do sistema político que não consegue falar com o eleitor", concluiu.

articles.title: 19-Year-Old Accused of Rape on College Campus, Less Than 2 Weeks After Another Student Was Arrested
articles.summary: Wichita State University student James Vandenberg, 19, was accused of rape 12 days after Aaron Christian, 18, was accused of the same crime
articles.body:
Two students at Wichita State University have been arrested and charged with rape in a span of 12 days

WSU student James Vandenberg, 19, was arrested on Sat., Oct. 24 and charged with rape

WSU student Aaron Christian, 18, was arrested on Oct. 12 and charged with aggravated domestic battery and rape

A 19-year-old Wichita State University student was arrested after being accused of for rape over the weekend, the second student to be arrested in connection with allegations of for sexual assault in less than two weeks, university police say.

On Saturday, Oct. 24, at 3:27 p.m., James Douglas Vandenberg, 19, was arrested and charged with one count of rape, university police said, KWCH and the university's student newspaper, The Sunflower, report.

Vandenberg was arrested at the dorms at the university in Wichita, per university police, the outlets report.

He was held at the Sedgwick County jail on $100,000 bond and was later released.

Vandenberg is a freshman who is studying business, The Sunflower reports. No other details of his arrest were available.

Vandenberg's arrest came less than two weeks after the arrest of another student, Aaron Andrew Christian, 18, who was arrested on Monday, Oct. 12, at 9:56 a.m., and faces charges of aggravated domestic battery and rape, university police allege, KWCH, The Sunflower and KAKE report.

Christian is no longer listed as an inmate at Sedgwick County Jail.

The sexual assault allegations against Christian were reported on campus on Sunday, Oct. 11, WSU Director of Communications Lainie Mazzullo-Hart said, KAKE reports.

Mazzullo-Hart said additional details would not be released because of privacy concerns and the ongoing investigation, according to KAKE.

In a statement, Wichita State University said "The university takes all reports of sexual assault seriously. Sexual violence has no place in any campus community, and we are committed to following all applicable laws, reporting, investigative and student-support processes," KWCH reports.

It is unclear whether Vandenberg or Christian have retained attorneys who can speak on their behalf.

University Police referred PEOPLE to the university's Strategic Communications Department, which did not immediately respond to PEOPLE's request for comment.

If you or someone you know has been a victim of sexual abuse, text "STRENGTH" to the Crisis Text Line at 741-741 to be connected to a certified crisis counselor.

articles.title: Texas Roadhouse Responds to Customer’s Viral Claims That He Was Given $20 Steak Instead of the $30 Cut He Ordered 3 Times
articles.summary: “While we can’t confirm this happened on multiple occasions, when Mr. Card brought this to our attention; it was made right by our team,” Texas Roadhouse tol...
articles.body:
Kenneth Card claimed that he was served a sirloin instead of the filet mignon he ordered on three separate occasions at a Texas Roadhouse in Forsyth, Ill.

Texas Roadhouse said Card's complaint was "made right" by its team and that it could not confirm multiple incidents.

Card, who says he used to work in restaurants, sparked an online debate after sharing a video detailing his experience.

A Texas Roadhouse customer is claiming that the restaurant served him a cheaper steak than he ordered.

On Oct. 5, Kenneth Card shared a TikTok video , which now has over 31,000 views, calling out the steakhouse chain and claiming he was served a less expensive steak than he ordered three times.

In his video, Card said he ordered an 8-oz. filet mignon at the Forsyth, Ill. location of the steakhouse chain before being served a sirloin steak instead.

"I said, 'Excuse me, I think I got the wrong steak,'" Card recalled in the video, adding that the server went to get a "second opinion" before returning and confirming it was a sirloin steak.

Card said he told the waiter he went to the restaurant weekly for a year, and this was the third time the issue occurred.

He told Fox News Digital the staff corrected the mistake the first time it happened, and that he didn't complain the second time it occurred.

Card said in his video that he told a manager it was the third time he received a sirloin instead of the filet he ordered.

He claimed that the manager looked at him as if he was "stupid or crazy" and said it was "impossible" because the steak goes through a manager in the back.

Card said when he brought up the current mistake, the manager was unable to respond.

"While we can't confirm this happened on multiple occasions, when Mr. Card brought this to our attention; it was made right by our team," a spokesperson for Texas Roadhouse said in a statement shared with PEOPLE.

"We have processes in place to double-check food for quality and accuracy before it leaves the kitchen," they added. "If a guest receives the wrong item or is charged incorrectly, we encourage them to let a member of our team know so we can make it right."

In his video, Card said that he was a cook "for many years" and had experience with handling steaks.

"I know [the] difference between a ribeye, a filet, a t-bone, New York strip, all that crap," he said in the video. "Whenever I go out to eat, I know what I get."

Card previously worked in hotel and restaurant kitchens, per Fox News Digital .

"Y'all be careful what y'all ordering and what you pay for because sometimes you order a filet, you'd be getting a sirloin," he told his viewers. "It's like a $10 steak versus $35."

Per the Texas Roadhouse location's website , an 8-oz. sirloin costs $19.49, and the 8-oz. Dallas filet costs $29.99.

"Talking about getting ripped off!" Card wrote in the caption of his TikTok, also writing in text overlaying the video, "Texas Roadhouse shame on you!"

Card did not immediately reply to PEOPLE's request for comment.

Some users sympathized with Card's position in the comments section of his video.

"This has been going on for years," one person claimed.

Another added, "They've done this to me many times. Ordered New York strip or ribeye and I get a sirloin."

However, others questioned Card's point of view.

"I've never had an issue with Texas roadhouse," one commenter wrote.

"Why do you keep going back if this continues to happen?" another asked.

"I think I'm done going in there," Card told Fox News Digital .

He told the outlet he wanted to ensure that customers got what they paid for.

articles.title: Built in 1911 for grocery heir Sess Cleveland and home to his family for 60 years, a 5,700 sq ft historic mansion on Houston’s Courtlandt Place that last sold in 2015 after being listed at $2.35 million is now on the market for nearly $4 million
articles.summary: A century-old mansion with ties to one of Houston’s prominent business families has returned to the property market, with an asking price of $3.995
articles.body: A century-old mansion with ties to one of Houston’s prominent business families has returned to the property market, with an asking price of $3.995 million. Located at 8 Courtlandt Place near the Montrose neighbourhood, the approximately 5,700-square-foot residence combines early 20th-century architecture with updated interiors and modern amenities. According to the property listing on Compass and reporting by the Houston Chronicle, the house was built in 1911 for Alexander Sessums Cleveland, known as Sess Cleveland, whose father helped establish one of Texas’s largest wholesale grocery businesses. The property last changed hands in 2015, when it was initially listed for $2.35 million. It is now being marketed as a historic residence within one of Houston’s distinctive gated residential enclaves.A mansion shaped by Houston’s business historyThe house was commissioned by Sess Cleveland and his wife, Virginia, at a time when Houston’s commercial fortunes were helping shape its most prestigious residential neighbourhoods. Sess was the son of William Davis Cleveland, a businessman who arrived in Houston in 1858 and built a successful career in wholesale groceries, cotton brokerage and civic affairs. The family business, W. D. Cleveland and Sons, became a major force in Texas’s grocery trade before closing in March 1930 during the Great Depression.The residence was designed by Sanguinet & Staats, an architectural firm known for its work across Texas. Houston architect John F. Staub later redesigned the property in the 1920s. Staub would go on to become closely associated with grand residential architecture in Houston, particularly in affluent neighbourhoods such as River Oaks. The Cleveland family remained in the house for approximately six decades, giving the property a long connection to the city's commercial and social history.Period details meet modern comfortsThe mansion’s appeal lies partly in the survival of its original architectural features. According to the listing details carried by the Houston Chronicle and real estate platforms, the interiors retain hardwood and parquet floors, plaster walls, period windows and traditional millwork.The formal living room features wood panelling and black marble detailing, while the dining room has a Texas limestone hearth. A separate library adds to the house’s traditional character, reflecting an era when dedicated reading and entertaining spaces were standard features of larger residences. The kitchen and butler’s pantry have been updated with quartzite countertops, custom cabinetry and premium Wolf and Sub-Zero appliances. Other features include updated bathrooms, custom closets, a screened porch and landscaped grounds with an outdoor entertaining area and fireplace.The property also has a basement, a four-car garage and a separate garage apartment. An original service staircase remains among the architectural details preserved in the house. The combination of historic finishes and contemporary upgrades gives prospective buyers a home that retains much of its original character without relying entirely on period facilities.Inside Courtlandt Place, Houston’s historic enclaveThe mansion sits on Courtlandt Place, a private residential street established in the early 20th century near Westheimer Road and Bagby Street. Planned in 1906, the enclave began taking shape with the construction of its first houses in 1909.Its collection of historic residences reflects the ambitions of Houston’s wealthy families during the city’s early growth. Architects associated with homes in the neighbourhood include Birdsall Briscoe, Alfred C. Finn and John F. Staub, whose work helped define the architectural character of the area. Courtlandt Place was added to the National Register of Historic Places in 1980. Its gated setting and concentration of early 20th-century houses distinguish it from the surrounding urban neighbourhoods.The street has continued to attract attention from luxury homebuyers. In July 2026, another property at 15 Courtlandt Place sold after being listed for $4.6 million, according to Houston Association of Realtors data reported by the Houston Chronicle. That sale demonstrated the continued interest in substantial historic homes within the enclave, although the final transaction price was not disclosed in the cited report.From $2.35 million to nearly $4 millionThe Cleveland mansion’s latest asking price represents a notable change from its previous appearance on the market. It was listed for $2.35 million in May 2015 before selling later that year. The current asking price of $3.995 million is about 70 per cent higher than its original 2015 listing price, although that comparison does not account for subsequent improvements, carrying costs or changes in market conditions.The listing offers a glimpse into a part of Houston’s residential history that has survived more than a century of urban change. For prospective buyers, the appeal extends beyond the size of the house or its upgraded kitchen: the property carries a direct connection to the Cleveland family and to the development of one of the city’s early luxury residential districts. As the mansion returns to the market, its combination of historical significance, preserved period details and modern amenities places it among the notable heritage properties currently available in Houston.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: France pledges education reforms after protests over costs, school funding
articles.summary: France’s government on Monday pledged to replace its national university admissions platform by 2028 and introduce a series of education reforms, seeking
articles.body: France’s government on Monday pledged to replace its national university admissions platform by 2028 and introduce a series of education reforms, seeking to address student grievances after weeks of protests over university access, school funding and the rising cost of living.Higher education minister Philippe Baptiste announced that the existing platform, Parcoursup, would undergo “substantial change” for the 2027 admissions round before being replaced the following year. The government also promised smaller classes, additional teaching posts, more higher education places, increased student grants and funding for building renovations.The concessions follow France’s worst unrest in years on October 17, when demonstrations over education and living costs escalated into rioting and looting. According to the Associated Press, protesters set fires, looted shops, clashed with police and attacked public buildings. Groups briefly stormed Marseille’s City Hall, while a fire at Limoges’ 19th-century town hall brought down its roof and clock tower.About 2,400 people were arrested in connection with the demonstrations, even as hundreds of thousands of people took part in peaceful marches. The movement, which began with school blockades in mid-September, has expanded beyond education to include workers demanding relief from rising living costs.Two high school student groups welcomed some of the government’s concessions but called for protests to continue, according to the AP. Their representatives met Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu earlier on Monday, before the government announced the measures. Further demonstrations are planned for October 31, followed by nationwide strikes and protests called by labour unions for November 5.Changes to ParcoursupParcoursup allows students to apply to universities and other higher education courses and receive admissions decisions. A record 1.05 million people applied through the platform this year, according to France’s higher education ministry.Students have criticised the system over what they describe as unclear selection criteria and unequal access to preferred courses. Under the changes announced for the 2027 admissions round, institutions would have to publish more detailed selection criteria. The platform would also provide explanatory information alongside rejections, while institutions would be required to give applicants the reasons for their decisions if asked.The government said a committee involving students and teachers would submit initial recommendations for a replacement system by the end of November. Legislation may be introduced if required to implement the proposed changes.The 2028 deadline, however, means the replacement system is unlikely to be delivered during president Emmanuel Macron’s current term. Macron cannot seek a third consecutive term in 2027, leaving the next president and government responsible for implementing the central promise.The AP reported that far-right leader Marine Le Pen was leading polling ahead of the first round of presidential voting scheduled for April 18, with a runoff planned for May 2. Her National Rally party has sought to capitalise on the unrest by presenting itself as a force for law and order and urging voters to channel their anger into support for her presidential bid.The replacement platform has yet to be designed, and possible legal changes remain unresolved, leaving key questions unanswered as the government tries to persuade students to end the protests.More places, grants and school fundingThe government also promised to create 15,000 additional places in higher education during 2027 and 2028, mainly in vocational and technical programmes. Student grants would be increased in line with inflation from the beginning of the 2027 academic year.To improve learning conditions, the government pledged to cap some first-year high school classes at 28 students from 2027, beginning with more disadvantaged schools. It also promised to reverse planned cuts to secondary-school teaching positions and create 500 additional jobs.The building plans extend beyond Macron’s presidency. The government proposed up to 4 billion euros ($4.5 billion) in low-interest loans to regional authorities for school renovations through 2030. A separate state plan worth 1 billion euros ($1.1 billion) would fund university renovations through 2029, according to the AP.The measures come as France faces record poverty and public debt, while demands for better-resourced schools have placed particular emphasis on disadvantaged communities.Earlier on Monday, Macron promised “concrete measures” to address students’ demands during a visit to Marseille, the southern port city. “I have asked the government to address the legitimate demands at the root of this protest movement,” he said.Macron and his centrist government have faced criticism over their response to student grievances since high school blockades began in mid-September. The protests have also prompted scrutiny of police crowd-control weapons, which have been blamed for life-changing injuries to some teenagers.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: No action on deleted voters using Form 6: Supreme Court
articles.summary: New Delhi: No one will be prosecuted for using Form 6 to re-enter their name in electoral rolls, the Supreme Court verbally assured electors on Monday.
articles.body: New Delhi: No one will be prosecuted for using Form 6 to re-enter their name in electoral rolls, the Supreme Court verbally assured electors on Monday. It allayed fears that use of Form 6, which asks applicants to declare they are fresh voters, for re-inclusion in draft electoral rolls could invite prosecution for false declaration.The statement came from a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohan while hearing a PIL against large-scale exclusion of names from Maharashtra’s draft electoral roll and as a response to senior advocate Aravind Datar’s plea that using Form 6 for re-inclusion would amount to lying under oath.Will grant time to genuine voters to submit papers if out from final list: SCThe bench also said that if it found there were genuine voters whose names could not be included in the final electoral list, to be published on Nov 6, it could grant them more time to submit their documents for the purpose. A similar concern was raised by advocate Prashant Bhushan 10 days earlier while questioning the EC’s directive that voters whose names were deleted from Delhi’s draft electoral roll during SIR exercise use Form 6 to restore them in draft rolls.Datar said that with two crore voters excluded from Maharashtra’s draft electoral roll, including 1.22 crore on grounds of logical discrepancy, and the deadline for claims and objections ending on Oct 26, many voters who were removed on flimsy and non-existent grounds would have little chance of getting names restored.The senior advocate requested the bench to extend the Oct-26 deadline for those seeking inclusion of their names in the electoral roll. The bench asked the EC to file its response to the PIL by Nov 5 and said it would examine on that day whether extra time would be required for those seeking inclusion of names.Datar said, “In Maharashtra, 33% of voters have been deleted. In Mumbai, 40% of the voters have been excluded. What is happening is people are asked to fill Form 6, which is meant for fresh voters. There is no provision for a person who had voted in the last three or four elections to get his name restored in the voter list. If he fills Form 6, which is meant for registration of fresh voters, then he would face prosecution for false declaration.”However, the CJI allayed these fears and said, “No one will be prosecuted for filling Form 6 seeking re-entering of their names in voter lists.” Datar said that since there was no imminent election in Maharashtra, the SC could direct EC not to finalise the electoral roll for the state on Nov 6 and postpone the schedule to enable genuine voters to re-enter them in voter lists. The bench also said, “If we find, even after the publication of the final electoral roll, that there are people who are genuine voters but still excluded, we can extend time for them to submit documents for the purpose of re-entering their names in voter lists.”Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Lawrence Bishnoi moved to high-security Ahemdabad jail block
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Gangster Lawrence Bishnoi is learnt to have been recently shifted to “Do sau kholi”, a specialised high-security block at Ahmedabad’s Sabarmati
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Gangster Lawrence Bishnoi is learnt to have been recently shifted to “Do sau kholi”, a specialised high-security block at Ahmedabad’s Sabarmati Central Jail housing 200 dangerous inmates accused of terrorism and other heinous offences, sources say. To ensure total isolation and prevent inter-cell movement, the block has four segregated sections of 50 prisoners each. The size of his cell is roughly 7.5x11 ft.The move is part of an elaborate security plan to clip the wings of Bishnoi.Lawrence put in block which also houses 2008 blasts convictsPrior to 2023-2024, Lawrence routinely made extortion calls, circulated threatening audio and video messages to manage his network and even gave interviews from different jails. But investigators have reported zero direct calls or communication originating from him over the past two years.Over the past two years, investigators have reported zero direct calls or communication originating from Lawrence Bishnoi.“Block 200” is a maximum-security area within Sabarmati jail which holds convicts of the 2008 serial blasts case and other serious cases and is generally the zone for prisoners convicted of serious offences and restrained from moving outside the prison under the provisions of Section 303 of the BNSS.Before this, Lawrence was held in “Dus Kholi,” a smaller high-security enclosure accommodating just 10 inmates. Prior to that, he was in Tihar jail and different jails in Punjab. Recorded calls of Lawrence threatening call centre owners and even a purported conversation with gangster Shehzad Bhatti had surfaced while he was in these jails.Deprived of physical interaction and digital access, Lawrence now lives under round-the-clock solitary surveillance. He reportedly maintains a disciplined, ascetic lifestyle inside his cell — spending mornings in meditation, regularly reciting the Hanuman Chalisa, observing fasts and maintaining a vegetarian diet. His only interactions with outside world involve attending court hearings via video conferencing and discussing his legal strategy with his lawyer.However, while he is isolated inside Sabarmati jail, his syndicate continues to operate globally through a decentralised chain of command. articles.title: Meet homeless man Anders Fernstedt, who has lived outside London’s £210 million mansion for 3.5 years; how he survives without money, sleeps through winters and why neighbours let him stay
articles.summary: A homeless man has been living outside one of London’s most expensive mansions for three and a half years, building an unusual home in one of the British
articles.body: A homeless man has been living outside one of London’s most expensive mansions for three and a half years, building an unusual home in one of the British capital’s wealthiest neighbourhoods. While the sprawling 45-room property remains empty, Anders Fernstedt has created a life for himself outside it, relying on donated food, clothes, books and a makeshift shelter.Located in Knightsbridge, the mansion at 2 to 8A Rutland Gate reportedly sold for £210 million in 2020. The property boasts views of Hyde Park, marble bathrooms, 116 windows and an indoor swimming pool. However, the buyer never moved in, leaving the luxurious property unoccupied for years.Fernstedt’s unusual living arrangement was explored in a video feature by DW Euromaxx, which followed him to understand how he ended up living outside the luxury property, how he manages without money and why some neighbours have accepted his presence.How Anders Fernstedt ended up homelessFernstedt was raised by his mother in Sweden and later pursued several careers in Sweden and the United States, establishing himself in the technology sector. He moved to England in 2016 and worked as a journalist and fact-checker before work dried up around the Covid-19 pandemic.A share in a technology company from his time in the US provided him with savings that he relied on for several years. However, as freelance commissions became harder to secure, his money gradually ran out.“There was enough money for me to live off for a few years, but only frugally, half the time in a tent,” he explained.Fernstedt said he slowly became accustomed to living on less, to the point that he did not immediately realise when he had effectively run out of money.“I slowly got used to frugality that I didn't even notice when I stopped having money,” he said.How he built a home outside a £210 million mansionFernstedt initially thought the spot outside the mansion would provide shelter for a night. Instead, it became his home for years.An avid camper with an interest in nature, he has adapted his outdoor space to suit his needs. He compares his makeshift shelter to a Mongolian yurt or other traditional tents, describing the imaginative way he has created a home on the mansion’s porch.He has also accumulated belongings that help him feel secure and comfortable. Comparing his collection to a squirrel storing nuts, Fernstedt explained that having several supplies means he does not immediately notice when something goes missing.His sleeping arrangements are particularly important to him. He has built up a collection of duvets and bedding, including what he described as seven layers of Hungarian down.“I haven't had a bad night's sleep for as long as I can remember,” he said, adding that his arrangements help him sleep through all four seasons.Fernstedt has learned to adapt to outdoor living, including London’s winters. He explained that sleeping without walls can also allow air to circulate during warmer weather.Why the neighbours let him stayLiving outside a mansion in one of London’s most exclusive neighbourhoods might appear difficult, but Fernstedt says he has gradually developed relationships with people in the surrounding community.After spending a few weeks at the location, he realised that residents knew he was there. He began thinking about how to make his presence familiar without intruding on their lives.He said he believed the neighbourhood’s children and grandchildren could help make his case to their families, hoping that conversations at home would encourage residents to accept him.Over time, some neighbours began approaching him to ask whether he needed anything. Their gestures have included food, clothes and even an elegant Italian dinner jacket.Fernstedt said that beyond material donations, he values ordinary human interaction and friendly conversations with the people living nearby.Not everyone in the neighbourhood has welcomed his presence, but he has found support from residents who appreciate his efforts to keep his makeshift home tidy and his lifestyle quiet. Some reportedly believe his presence may also help deter thieves or vandals from targeting the empty property.The feature does not establish that Fernstedt has formal permission or a legal right to remain outside the mansion.How he manages without money, electricity or basic amenitiesFernstedt describes himself as being almost completely disconnected from money. His daily expenses are minimal, with filter coffee among the few things he says he pays for.For essentials such as showers, food and clothing, he relies partly on charitable support. He visits a charity near Victoria that provides showers, a canteen and access to donated clothing and other basic necessities.The support helps him obtain everyday items, including socks, while occasional gifts from neighbours offer additional assistance.Without a conventional electricity supply, Fernstedt relies on several portable power banks to keep his devices running. He uses his phone to download books, including history titles and the diaries of filmmaker Andrei Tarkovsky.His collection of books and personal belongings offers a sense of continuity in a life that otherwise operates far removed from conventional housing and employment.Why he says he finally feels at homeFernstedt’s current arrangement has given him a sense of security that he says he did not always experience in temporary accommodation.After living at the location for years, he no longer constantly worries that his belongings will disappear while he is away.“Because I've been here so long, I'm free of worrying now, and if we worry too much, we won't be happy,” he said.You use AI every day. Farahnak alleged that Comey directed staff to speak to Savage about specific accuracy concerns relating to the Reuters report, thereby transferring classified information illegally.The charges add to the legal cases involving Comey, who has remained a prominent target of Trump’s criticism since their clash over the FBI’s investigation into Russian election interference in 2016.You use AI every day. articles.title: June 2025 decision to hold SIR taken unanimously, EC tells SC
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Election Commission Monday filed an affidavit in SC that the chief election commissioner and the two election commissioners had unanimously
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Election Commission Monday filed an affidavit in SC that the chief election commissioner and the two election commissioners had unanimously taken the decision on June 24, 2025 to conduct nationwide SIR of electoral rolls and that there was no difference of opinion.The affidavit by deputy EC Bhanu Prakash Yeturu came with an unusual declaration that it was being filed with the approval of the CEC and the two ECs. “At the very outset, I state that the present affidavit has been approved for filing before the SC by a unanimous decision of the three members of the Election Commission, that is the 2 election commissioners and the chief election commissioner,” the affidavit said.The assertion contradicts the charge that CEC Gyanesh Kumar, at Modi government’s instance, unilaterally decided to conduct SIR of electoral rolls — the mainstay of the opposition’s “vote chori” campaign.The affidavit was filed in response to petitions, including one filed by Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders, following a news report that the two ECs — S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi — had approached the cabinet secretary because of their differences with the CEC over SIR-related issues.“Allegations based on the communication between ECs and the cabinet secretary are misconceived,” the EC said, adding that the letters by Sandhu and Joshi pertained to administrative matters.No substance in claim that Form 6 was amended by SIR orders: ECAn office order came to be issued on July 28 by an IAS officer of the rank of additional secretary who had been posted on deputation to the commission pertaining to internal work allocation. On July 29, the two election commissioners wrote separate letters to the cabinet secretary in relation to this order and the conduct of the officer. In view of the joint direction of July 30 by the two ECs, the order of July 28 was never implemented,” the commission said. Responding to the petitions by Rahul and other INDIA bloc netas, the EC said all the petitions were based on a news article alleging that the commission had not been functioning in accordance with the procedure mandated in law, and allegations were also made questioning the integrity of the commission.It also issued a strong denial of the allegation, another key plank of the opposition’s offensive, that Form 6, as provided under Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, was amended by the commission by the SIR orders of June 24 and Oct 27 last year and May 14 this year. “There is no substance in the contention that Form 6 has been amended by the commission vide the SIR orders.” EC said Form 6 could be amended only by the Centre and what was changed was the introduction of a declaration to “enable the person seeking registration as a voter to dispense with the need for filing documents during the claims and objections period”.The ‘declaration’ was a document provided by the SIR orders and was not a part of Form 6, which was the statutory form for inclusion in the electoral rolls, it said, adding there was no significant change in the earlier and present declaration. The declaration that the affidavit was approved by the two ECs is significant because of the charge that the CEC’s “unilateral” calls on SIR-related issues were violative of the law, which required the poll body to take decisions unanimously or, when not possible, by majority. The opposition has demanded removal and prosecution of Gyanesh Kumar for violating the law.Denying the charge, the affidavit said that while the CEC, the ECs and even other officers may have expressed different views during deliberations, the decisions were taken in accordance with law. “The views by ECs/CEC of the commission during the decision-making process on the subjects before them are considered for arriving at the decision. It is upon consideration of all the views placed before the commission that the decision is taken and the orders are issued in accordance with the process,” the EC said.Explaining the process of decision-making in which views of all divisions concerned with the subject are considered in detail, the EC said, “In any such decision-making process, any suggestion, observation or query by the CEC or ECs either to the ECs or CEC or to any officer of the commission does not constitute a decision of the commission under Section 18 of the CEC and ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023.”It said the statute prefers a decision by unanimity but also provides for decision-making by majority in the three-member EC. The commission said the CEC and ECs had taken a unanimous decision on June 29 that “in case any person to whom notice has been issued during the ongoing SIR, for being unmapped and/or logical discrepancies, BLOs will visit the homes of such persons for collection of documents and thereafter upload them in the ECINet, for decision by the ERO”.“Such person shall not be called for hearing to the ERO/AERO officer. Only in exceptional circumstances, as defined by the ERO/AERO, will the hearing be held, preferably online. Any adult member of the family can be authorised by the elector to attend the hearing on their behalf,” EC said. Referring to the allegation relating to deletion of 97 voters in Goa, the commission said it had directed that no eligible voter should be left out of the rolls and pursuant to this, the BLOs conducted a house-to-house visit and found that 88 of the 97 had already filled Form 6 for inclusion of their names. Of the remaining nine, six were out of the country and three were Portuguese passport holders.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: In 2026, two companies sued a Nevada county over a data-centre ban affecting 911 acres; they say officials changed the rules after years of planning
articles.summary: Two companies have sued Nye County in Nevada after officials banned data centre development across the Pahrump Valley and the surrounding groundwater
articles.body: Two companies have sued Nye County in Nevada after officials banned data centre development across the Pahrump Valley and the surrounding groundwater basin in August 2026. The dispute centres on nearly 911 acres of land intended for the proposed Manse Technology Campus, a large technology project that its developers say had already undergone years of planning. The companies argue that county officials changed the rules after they had invested heavily in the development. The lawsuit now challenges the legality of the ban and raises questions about landowners’ rights.Why did the Nevada data centre ban lead to a lawsuitAccording to KTNV, the companies involved in the legal dispute are CDDC, LLC and 9 of a Kind, LLC. Together, they own nearly 911 acres along Carpenter Canyon Road and Nevada State Route 160, where they had planned to establish the Manse Technology Campus, also known as the MTC Project.The developers claim they moved forward with the project because existing county zoning rules and guidance from officials indicated that development could proceed. They argue that their plans followed the applicable requirements, including changes made to county zoning rules in 2023.The dispute intensified when the Nye County Board of Commissioners voted on August 18, 2026, to prohibit data centres in the Pahrump area and Water Basin 162. The decision affected the location selected for the proposed campus.KTNV said the companies believe the county's decision undermined their property rights after they had committed substantial resources to the project.Developer Sean Dalesandro also told KTNV that the project had proceeded in reliance on the county's zoning framework and the guidance received during the planning process. The companies are asking the court to review whether officials could lawfully change the rules in these circumstances.What was planned for the Manse Technology CampusThe Manse Technology Campus had become a source of local debate even before the lawsuit was filed. The proposal attracted attention because large data centres can require substantial infrastructure, including electricity supplies, cooling equipment and water resources.A report by the Pahrump Valley Times described efforts by the project's proponents to address residents' concerns. The developers planned to hold an informational meeting to discuss the proposal and engage with the local community.The controversy reflected a wider debate about whether large technology facilities are suitable for areas where residents are concerned about the availability of natural resources and the effects of industrial development.For the developers, the project represented an investment opportunity tied to the growing demand for facilities that support digital services. For residents concerned about its potential effects, however, the proposal raised questions about how such developments should be assessed and regulated.How did county officials change the rulesThe dispute developed against a background of changing county policy on data centre construction.According to Nye's Lies, which examined the court filing in an October 1, 2026, report, the companies filed their petition on September 11, less than a month after the county adopted the ban. Their case seeks to have Ordinance No. 631 overturned.The report said the companies claim they spent millions of dollars on engineering work for the proposed development. They also point to the county's handling of their application, including the payment of a fee in June and the receipt of comments on their plans in August.The companies argue that these steps, together with the guidance they received, supported their expectation that the project could move forward.However, the account published by Nye's Lies also highlighted an important distinction. The available planning steps did not necessarily amount to final approval of the data centre itself. The land still required relevant planning changes and rezoning, and the development agreement sought by the companies had not been formally approved by the county commission.This distinction is central to the dispute. The developers argue that the county's conduct and existing zoning framework justified their investment, while the legal question includes whether those circumstances created an enforceable right to proceed.What does the ban mean for other data centre projectsNye County's decision forms part of a wider debate across Nevada about how local governments should regulate data centre construction.The state has seen several local authorities consider different approaches to managing development. Reno introduced a temporary moratorium on new data centre construction permits in May 2026 and extended it in June, while Henderson rejected a proposed temporary moratorium in July.Nye County's August decision was particularly significant because it prohibited data centres in the Pahrump Valley and the Water Basin 162 groundwater area. The new regulations also cover data centre development outside Pahrump's Basin 162.The lawsuit seeks to challenge the county's ban and obtain judicial review of the decisions affecting the development. They also challenge the county's zoning designation for their property, arguing that it is too vague and could allow arbitrary enforcement.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.summary: Twitch personality Blaire “QTCinderella” is facing mounting criticism after an online user accused her of filing multiple false copyright complaints
articles.body: Twitch personality Blaire “QTCinderella” is facing mounting criticism after an online user accused her of filing multiple false copyright complaints against social media accounts sharing clips of her content. The allegations have drawn reactions from prominent streamers, including Asmongold and Dan Saltman, turning a dispute over online videos into a wider debate about creator rights and freedom of expression. With claims of 10 takedown notices circulating and questions about fair use gaining attention, the controversy has put the host of The Streamer Awards under fresh scrutiny. QTCinderella had not publicly responded to the allegations at the time of reporting.QTCinderella DMCA allegations spark backlash over 10 takedown noticesThe controversy gained traction on October 24, 2026, after X user @Awk20000 claimed that QTCinderella had issued repeated copyright complaints against accounts posting clips from 2025. The user alleged that they had received 10 takedown notices and argued that short clips could qualify as fair use, depending on how they were used.In the post, the user wrote:"QTCinderella has been sending out mass false DMCA takedowns to channels, including mine. I have received 10 of these takedowns from clips in 2025. Clipping small segments is absolutely fair use @qtcinderella is one of the few creators who will try to continually silence others with lawfare, having done this before. If this was a mistake or misidentification, hopefully she can retract it."Another X user, @bloomjpg, shared screenshots of an email from X Legal Support stating that content had been removed following a complaint attributed to QTCinderella.The claims have not been independently established, and a copyright takedown does not automatically prove that a complaint was fraudulent or that the disputed material qualifies as fair use. That distinction matters because copyright disputes depend on the specific content, its purpose and how it was used.Kick streamer Dan Saltman offered to help the accuser challenge the notices, promising financial support for a potential legal fight."I will cover 100% of your legal costs to fight this, will dm you. Its so funny how this side always acts like they are above lawfare but will do it for anything that makes them look bad. @qtcinderella withdraw the DMCA's- I am kinda busy atm!"Asmongold criticises QTCinderella over alleged copyright strikesAs the dispute spread, streamer Asmongold addressed the allegations during a livestream on October 25. He argued that copyright complaints against people sharing clips can damage a creator's relationship with their audience."'This is a terrible look.' Yeah. This is just awful. But anyway, anybody who tries to do this, I will definitely say this - anybody who tries to file DMCAs will almost always have the reverse happen, where now you turn your entire community against you. Because, fundamentally, the people on the internet want to choose what they can and can't see, and they don't want creators trying to take away their ability to do that. They don't want creators that are trying to massage the narrative and mislead them into thinking that one thing is real, where it's actually something else."Asmongold also urged QTCinderella to apologise and withdraw the disputed complaints."So, again, this is just a huge mistake, and I think that she should completely apologize and remove this. But DMCA-ing people for posting clips about you that make you look bad is absolutely embarrassing. It's totally embarrassing, and I think it's also illegal. It's illegal because you're not considering fair use."The controversy remains unresolved. Until QTCinderella responds or further evidence emerges, the accusations should be treated as claims rather than established facts. articles.summary: Top officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan met Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday in a bid to de-escalate the conflict in West Asia, as
articles.body: Top officials from Saudi Arabia, Turkiye and Pakistan met Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday in a bid to de-escalate the conflict in West Asia, as Yemen’s Houthis launched new attacks on Saudi Arabia and Egypt approved defence support for the Gulf kingdom. The talks were the first high-level contact between Iran and the three nations — which signed the Mecca mutual defence pact in Aug — since a war that began with US and Israeli strikes on Iran also spread to Saudi Arabia and Yemen.The Saudi foreign ministry said the visit was intended to open negotiating channels to “prevent the return of military escalation”. Saudi Arabia was represented by defence minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, younger brother of Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman; Pakistan by army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir; and Turkiye by intelligence chief Ibrahim Kalin, Saudi and Iranian officials said.Iranian state media published pictures of Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, foreign minister Abbas Araqchi and Mohsen Rezaei, secretary of the Supreme National Security Council, attending the meetings. At the conclusion of the meetings, the four states agreed to continue talks with a view to strengthening cooperation, especially in peace and security, state media reported.Pakistan and Qatar have led mediation efforts in the war. Qatari mediators were in Tehran Sunday, an official said.Earlier efforts helped produce an interim peace agreement in June but fighting between Iran and the United States soon resumed. Conflict then flared between the Iran-aligned Houthis and US ally Saudi Arabia, opening a new front.Iranian foreign ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said Monday’s discussions would include “Israel’s expansionist policies, developments in the Palestinian territories and Lebanon, and the repercussions of US and Israeli military action against Iran”.Egypt parl okays defence support for SaudisSaudi Arabia has intensified strikes against the Houthis since they captured strategic areas along Yemen’s Red Sea coast last month, advancing against Saudi-backed govt forces. The Houthis have hit Saudi airports, ports and oil installations. On Monday, the Houthis said they had attacked pumping stations on Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline as well as Riyadh airport. There was no immediate Saudi confirmation of the Houthi attacks. The parliament in Egypt, which has said it is considering joining the Mecca pact, Monday authorised the Egyptian military to help defend Saudi Arabia, a major financial and political partner for Cairo.‘Hezbollah readies for new war with funds from Iran’Lebanese armed group Hezbollah has spent three months preparing for a possible resumption of hostilities with Israel, after receiving an infusion of cash from Iran, according to Lebanese security personnel briefed on its activities. Invading Israeli forces now occupy its heartland of villages in southern Lebanon, and political pressure has built up in Beirut for its disarmament. It nevertheless remains committed to fighting Israel and has used a lull in hostilities since June to rearm, with a focus on procuring explosives and producing drones that can be flown into Israeli positions, two Lebanese security sources said.One of the sources, and another close to Hezbollah, said the group had received millions of dollars from Iran to help boost its military capabilities. The group has been restoring command-and-control structures that broke down in key battles, according to one of those sources and three other security officials familiar with the group's operations.You use AI every day. articles.title: More violence in Arunachal as anti-dam protests spread
articles.summary: PASIGHAT/ITANAGAR: A 12-hour bandh against a proposed hydropower project in Arunachal Pradesh’s Upper Subansiri district turned violent Monday, with mobs
articles.body: PASIGHAT/ITANAGAR: A 12-hour bandh against a proposed hydropower project in Arunachal Pradesh’s Upper Subansiri district turned violent Monday, with mobs damaging vehicles and NHPC equipment and wounding two security personnel as anti-dam protests spread from Siang basin to Subansiri valley, report Kangkan Kalita and Joken Ete.The latest flashpoint was Daporijo town, 220km west of Pasighat by road. NHPC equipment, a company vehicle and two police vehicles were damaged during the bandh called by All Tagin Students’ Union and other organisations against Menga dam, part of the proposed 1,605MW Subansiri Upper Hydroelectric Project. Police conducted a flag march in Daporijo and appealed for peace.Remove central forces, say protesters; depends on restoration of peace: GovernmentConstable-driver Hibu Lasha and a CRPF man were wounded. Both were shifted to Ziro for treatment,” Upper Subansiri SP Pawan Kumar Yadav said.The bandh began at 5am over opposition to the proposed Menga dam and an alleged attempt to detain ATSU president Tadak Pakba. Backed by student unions and community groups from the Subansiri basin, the agitation grew out of fears that the project would threaten their land, livelihoods, and future.Earlier, Pasighat recorded widespread arson, vandalism and clashes with security forces when protesters laid siege to the East Siang district headquarters from Friday night to early Saturday over the proposed 11,200 MW Siang Upper Multipurpose Project (SUMP), with its main reservoir planned near Geku village, about 35km downstream from Upper Siang district headquarters Yingkiong.The Siang flows from Tibet into the ancestral land of the Adi community inhabiting Siang, Upper Siang and East Siang districts, while Upper Subansiri is home to the Tagin community. The Adi and Tagin people are closely related.Tension continued in Upper Siang, where protesters demanded the release of people arrested for the violence and four activists placed under preventive detention. articles.title: In 2024, a California walnut farmer turned a small email experiment into a major change in his business: Just 300 of 10,000 cherry customers opted in, yet direct sales helped triple his walnut crop's gross revenue
articles.summary: A simple email marketing test launched in 2024 became a major business success for a California walnut farmer.
articles.body: A simple email marketing test launched in 2024 became a major business success for a California walnut farmer. It showed how selling directly to customers can greatly increase farm income. The farmer first contacted a list of 10,000 people who had bought cherries from his orchard in the past. From that large group, only 300 people chose to receive updates and direct offers for his upcoming walnut harvest. Despite the small number of customers who signed up, those 300 buyers helped the farmer build a direct sales business. In the end, he tripled the total gross revenue from his walnut crop. The strategy reflects a growing trend among specialty crop farmers looking for alternatives to traditional wholesale sales. By selling directly to households, growers can earn more from each sale and protect their businesses from changes in wholesale prices.Direct sales boost crop returnsCommercial nut farmers usually rely on wholesalers and processors to buy and distribute their seasonal crops. These businesses can handle large amounts of produce, but farmers remain exposed to changing market prices, processing fees and lower payments for their crops. In 2024, the California farmer tested whether the customer relationships he had built during cherry season could help him sell walnuts, too. Cherries are often an impulse purchase during the summer, but he found that customers who enjoyed buying fruit directly from his farm were also interested in purchasing fresh walnuts. Of the 10,000 cherry customers who received an email, only 300 signed up for the separate walnut mailing list. However, these 300 subscribers were committed buyers who were willing to purchase directly from the farm at retail prices. By selling to this focused group, the farmer earned more per pound than he would have through wholesale markets. The extra money from direct sales was enough to triple the total gross revenue from his entire walnut harvest.Farm economics shift away from wholesaleSelling produce directly to customers means handling packaging, processing orders and shipping products to homes. However, the higher earnings are encouraging more farmers to try this approach. Under standard wholesale agreements, farmers deliver their crops to processors. The final amount they receive depends on global supplies and market demand. In years with large harvests or trade barriers, wholesale prices can fall close to the cost of growing the crops. Direct sales allow farmers to set prices based on the quality of their crops, freshness and shipping costs. For small and medium-sized orchards, selling even part of their yearly harvest directly to customers can help make income more stable. The results of the 2024 campaign showed that farmers do not need a huge customer base to improve their earnings. A small list of interested, repeat buyers can generate enough sales to make an entire crop much more profitable.Building long-term customer relationshipsThe farmer's experience shows how important it is to keep customers and build a reliable contact list in modern agriculture. Collecting 10,000 customer contacts took work during cherry harvest season. However, turning some of those buyers into customers throughout the year created a repeatable way to sell other crops. By keeping in touch through email, the farmer built a steady sales channel and reduced his dependence on outside brokers. Industry analysts point out that direct sales can help specialty crop farmers manage financial risks.
